key_insight: ARGUS is an evidence-constrained agentic framework that separates deterministic genomic analysis from LLM reasoning to reduce hallucinated interpretations of noncoding variants.
clinical_relevance: It may improve how researchers prioritize and interpret regulatory variants in genomic medicine by grounding claims in real experimental and annotation evidence rather than model-only guesses.
method: Uses 458 DNABERT-based TF-binding models as deterministic predictors.
A planner selects evidence sources based on uncertainty, while a verifier interprets each result and updates the investigation path.
Integrates real ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE queries in a hypothesis-directed loop.
evidence_signal: In the rs6983267 case study, ARGUS produced divergent TF-specific trajectories and used real evidence to support or abstain from claims, including ADASTRA results (e.g., 15 experiments, FDR = 0.030 for FOXA1; 5 experiments, FDR = 0.65 for RAD21).
watch_item: Performance depends on the coverage and quality of available external evidence, so some variants may still end in abstention when direct data are sparse or inconclusive.
paper_title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
